  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study quantifies the concordance of gene expression signatures between mouse models and human patients in response to inflammation and sepsis, using statistical measures of overlap and enrichment. It explicitly compares animal model results to human clinical outcomes.",
  "arm": "disease-biology",
  "arm_evidence": "Compendium of Immune Signatures Identifies Conserved and Species-Specific Biology in Response to Inflammation",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "sepsis-inflammation",
    "infectious-disease"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "Compendium of Immune Signatures Identifies Conserved and Species-Specific Biology in Response to Inflammation",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "ImmuneSigDB included data from healthy human subjects, patients with immune or non-immune diseases, and mouse models.",
  "species": [
    "mouse",
    "multiple-aggregated"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "Mapping orthologous genes to a common identifier allowed us to include both human (n = 135) and mouse (n = 254) studies",
  "endpoint_class": "secondary-biomarker",
  "endpoint_evidence": "Analysis using ImmuneSigDB identified signatures induced in activated myeloid cells and differentiating lymphocytes that were highly conserved between humans and mice."
